..
Issued at 315 AM CDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Vigorous upper trough evident on water vapor imagery early this 
morning moving into the upper Mississippi Valley. The associated 
surface cold front has now pushed east of the CWA with gusty 
northwesterly winds ushering in a colder and less humid air mass. 
Showers associated with the cold front will move east of our CWA 
well before sunrise, however additional scattered showers are 
expected this afternoon in association with the mid-upper level 
trough moving across the area. Despite the drier low level air mass 
advecting in, a pocket of very cold air aloft associated with the 
trough (-27C at 500mb on 00z Bismark sounding) will aid in 
destabilization and support scattered showers this afternoon. While 
scattered showers are expected area wide late this morning into this 
afternoon, the arrival of the cold air aloft should result in a 
significant increase in lake induced instability resulting in more 
widespread and robust showers over Lake Michigan spreading into 
northwest Indiana (mainly east of Gary). Forecast soundings depict 
the top of the moist convective layer reaching above the -20C level 
this afternoon over southern Lake Michigan, which could even allow 
an isolated thunderstorm or two. 

The cloud cover, scattered showers, and strong cold air advection 
should result in very little diurnal recovery in temperatures with 
temperatures holding nearly steady in the upper 40s to mid 50s. 
Strong and gusty northwest winds will only add to the chill with 
gusts over 30 mph likely today. Lake induced instability and less 
friction will result in even stronger winds over Lake Michigan 
bleeding onto the northwest Indiana shore this afternoon into early 
this evening when a few gusts to around 45 mph are expected. 

Skies clear out early this evening and winds will gradually subside 
tonight, the exception being into northwest Indiana where lake 
effect showers will likely continue. The lake cloudiness and showers 
will keep temps relatively milder over northwest Indiana, but else 
look for the coldest night thus far this autumn. Have upgraded the 
freeze watch to a freeze warning and expanded it a bit farther south 
and east. Have buffered the freeze warning with a frost advisory for 
a couple of counties, though admittedly, tonight doesn't look 
particularly favorable for frost. Winds will be slow to subside, 
though over our western CWA very late tonight we could see winds get 
close to decoupling. The winds should prevent strong radiational 
cooling and with T/Td spreads expected to remain at or above 5F, 
frost potential is pretty iffy tonight. Nonetheless, with temps 
progged to get close to freezing and winds subsiding toward sunrise, 
felt it was prudent to hoist a frost advisory out of an abundance of 
caution and as a hedge in case temps were to get colder and dip to 
or just below freezing. 

As the sharp upper trough shifts east of the region later tonight, 
inversion heights will come crashing down and should shut down the 
lake effect showers by or just shortly after sunrise Saturday. 
Outside of the decreasing lake effect cloudiness downwind of the 
lake Sat AM, look for sunny skies this weekend. Light winds with the 
still chilly air mass in place should result in below average temps 
in the 50s for highs Saturday. Saturday night the frost/freeze 
potential looks greatest away from the immediate lakeshore in 
northwest Indiana where strong radiational cooling is expected. 
Frost/freeze headlines will likely be needed Saturday night for at 
least portions of northwest Indiana and perhaps west into portions 
of northern IL as well. 

Our impending cold snap looks to be short lived with warm air 
advection ramping up Sunday and highs rebounding back into the 60s. 
Unseasonably mild weather is expected next week with highs 
approaching 70 Monday and likely in the 70s the rest of the week. 
Average highs next week drop into the upper 50s, so we'll be looking 
at high temps 10 to nearly 20F above average by the middle and end 
of next week. After the shower threat ends over most of the area 
late this afternoon and downwind of the lake by early Saturday, no 
precipitation is expected through the rest of the weekend and next 
week looks dry as well.

- Izzi
